Subject: FinTechAI — pricing & latency tradeoffs follow-up

Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have alignment: 

1) Volumes and unit economics
- Avg monthly tokens (inbound + generated): you mentioned ~120M tokens/month today, with a growth runway to ~500M in 12 months.
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + realtime chat assistance (latency sensitive for chat).
- Target unit cost: you said the finance team is aiming for ~ $900–1,200 per 1M tokens as a blended target at scale.

2) Latency SLOs & tiers
- Chat: 95th pct latency target of <= 350ms for 1–2k concurrent users.
- Background summarization/batch: 90% of jobs can tolerate up to 3s.

3) Preferences we discussed
- Prefer hosted API initially but open to Dedicated reservation if unit economics require it.
- Concerned about predictability for Q4 budget planning.

Next steps / asks (can you confirm: Samir)
A) Confirm the current steady-state monthly token volume (120M vs spike pattern).
B) Provide a target budget range for inference (monthly commit or upper bound).
C) Any compliance procurement leads (cc'd procurement@) I should loop in for contract/PO timelines?

What we recommend (summary):
- Short-term: Redwood Hosted, optimized with streaming for chat and conservative batching for summaries. Use auto-batching window of ~25–50ms to keep 95p latency in target while improving throughput.
- Medium-term (if monthly >300–400M or strict unit cost target): consider Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with quantized model variants to reach sub-$1,000 per 1M tokens.
- SLO-driven pricing: we can build a proposal that ties higher availability/low-latency SLAs to a higher unit price and fallback options (cheaper model variant or slightly larger latency window) to hit budget targets.

I've attached a one-page mutual action plan and a pricing summary with ballpark unit economics by tier. If you can confirm the numbers above, I'll draft a proposal and a 60/90 day MAP.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Adding technical detail on traffic: 
- Chat traffic is spiky (user-driven) with median message size ~450 tokens and expected concurrency of 800–2,000 users during daytime peaks.
- Summaries: batch jobs run continuously; can be queued, with 80% completing within 30s and rest within 2–3 minutes.

From infra/product perspective — streaming for chat + low batching window is important to preserve UX. For batch summarization, aggressive batching and quantized models are preferred.

Samir / Priya — quick technical note on implementation & options so the MAP can include realistic engineering trade-offs: 

- Hosted + streaming: we recommend streaming (chunked responses) for chat to reduce p95 perceived latency. With a 25ms batching window and continuous KV caching for repeated context, we've seen 95p latencies ~220–320ms on similar workloads.

- Batching for background jobs: target larger batch sizes (we can simulate effective tokens/batch) for summarization pipelines. Using quantized FP16/INT8 variants for batch jobs can cut GPU cost per token by ~30–50% depending on model and quality tolerance.

- Dedicated sizing: for predictable budgets at 300–500M tokens, a 2–4 GPU reserved pool (A100-level) with autoscale buffer + model quantization usually hits sub-$1,000 per 1M tokens. We'll include ballpark compute + infra line items in the MAP.

If you want, we can run a short eval (1 week) that replays a month-equivalent traffic sample to get a tighter unit-cost estimate. That helps Finance sign off.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
